BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Playbook. The Seller documents are treated as untrusted counterparty material.

## Threshold observations

1. **The Seller's labels carry no weight.** The draft calls its positions "fair and balanced", "agreed price mechanics", "considered adequate" and "settled". None of these has been confirmed through our authority process (playbook s 0.4 / 6.3).
2. **The facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Every factual item needs a bring-down: Bluefen, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment, the DD-006 investigation and Sandbar status. Until updated, these are Seller assertions, not verified facts.
3. **No fallback authority exists.** Amelia Frost has given no written authority for any fallback. Where a Seller number matches a fallback (the 20% cap and the 18-month period), that does not clear it.

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price, being AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25%, being AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given. Matching the fallback number does not clear it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25,000. Basket of AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of AUD 5,000. Basket of AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** Reject and restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k with a tipping basket.
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure permanently loses the first AUD 250k of loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. It also proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Reason:** 18 months is an unauthorised fallback, and the default rule silently imports the general time bar into Title, Tax, IP, indemnity and covenant claims.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and a period of at least six years. These claims should sit outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for, so they cannot be capped at AUD 4.8m or time-barred at 18 months.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5). There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert an express carve-out in each of cl 9.3, 12.x, 13 and 20.5.
- **Reason:** This is non-negotiable under the playbook and no one may waive it. As drafted, the clauses purport to protect the Seller even against its own fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 22 September 2026 (cl 1.1). It also discloses the Accounts, the statutory registers and public corporate records (cl 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 1.1 and 1.2. Accept only specific disclosures that are fair, identify the warranty affected and give enough detail to assess the matter. Also limit the reservation in cl 1.4 so it cannot dilute specific disclosures.
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure shifts the entire diligence risk to us.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it must:
  - be a Seller-knowledge qualifier tied to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; and
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reason:** As drafted, it combines constructive knowledge with deemed disclosure and would neutralise most warranties.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** "Addressed". The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the consent deemed satisfied on delivery of a written consent (cl 3 / 6.3). Its own Disclosure Letter (item 2) admits there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion as a condition precedent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make an effective Bluefen consent with satisfied conditions a CP, and add a Buyer walk-right if it is not obtained.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m). Reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are insufficient for a customer that material. The "addressed" claim also contradicts the Seller's own disclosure.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion". The Disclosure Letter (item 3) states the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds, as a funds flow line item; and
  - executed security releases (including PPSR discharge) delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-completion release.
- **Reason:** A post-completion release needs both an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and we have neither. Without the release we would take the shares with the bank's security and change-of-control rights (cl 8.1) still live.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter (item 5) is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs either shown as a specific funds flow / Debt line item or funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require the line item, or a Seller deduction with a specific indemnity. Ask the Seller to quantify the on-costs.
- **Reason:** These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion. Leaving them out of the funds flow silently transfers them to the Buyer.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader IP indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. It should cover:
  - failure of transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3;
  - third-party claims; and
  - costs of procuring a confirmatory assignment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow form.
- **Reason:** Transfer of the Project Materials depends on cleared payment, and the data room contains neither a receipt nor a confirmatory assignment. The AUD 180,000 open figure in DD-010 is not independently verified in either direction. We should not assume it is owed or that it has been paid.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - preservation of logs;
  - a completed investigation;
  - pre-Completion update obligations; and
  - specific protection for the incident.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the materiality characterisation. Require log preservation, investigation, a bring-down update covering the period since 22 September, and a specific indemnity for this incident.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 records may be affected and access, scope and notification duty are all unresolved. We should not assert a confirmed breach, harm or a dollar figure, and we should not accept "immaterial" either.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** The three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment, with no automatic conclusion either way.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the ordinary-course label yet. Request the following for DD-008 and DD-011, read together:
  - timing;
  - terminability;
  - accrual status; and
  - whether each renewal was entered in the ordinary course.

  Then decide whether any portion is Debt-like.
- **Reason:** The Disclosure Letter (item 8) itself does not state these facts. We should not pre-emptively classify the renewals as Debt or claim a price deduction.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** The draft applies limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to all Claims. It sets "all Claims unless expressly stated" as the default, and folds Title, Tax and IP into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, with no hidden override from the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Draft each category's limitations expressly and add a clause stating that the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- **Reason:** The Seller's catch-all drafting is the mechanism that collapses every protected category into the AUD 4.8m / 18-month bucket.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. This means:
  - an ASIC extract;
  - PPSR searches over Seller and Company;
  - share certificates and transfer history;
  - Seller board approvals and authority; and
  - no-encumbrance confirmation, including any Riverlark share security.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DD-012 as sufficient.
- **Reason:** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller. The Disclosure Letter (item 10) itself concedes it is not Buyer verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** These terms treated as OPEN.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled". Record Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.
- **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process. We should not assume resolution and should not table unlimited liability as our ask.

## Summary and next steps

| Issue | Status |
|---|---|
| 001–016 | All Seller positions rejected or not accepted as drafted |
| 005 (Fraud) | Non-waivable, highest priority |
| 008, 009, 010, 015 | Completion-critical (CP, funds flow and title deliverables) |

**Next steps:**
1. Issue a Buyer mark-up reflecting the playbook starting positions.
2. Send a bring-down information request covering all factual items as at a current date.
3. Make no use of the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying this draft.
